characterization_methods: High angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM)
evidence: Specifically, the nanostructure and nanochemistry of the PEALD Ta2O5/SiOx/Si stack and the electrical properties of the films are characterized using cross-sectional high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), high angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) equipped with parallel electron energy loss spectrometer, and capacitance-voltage (C-V) and leakage-current–voltage (JL-V) techniques. Additionally, JL-V and oxide breakdown statistics are carried out to compare the defect densities between ALD and PEALD Ta2O5 films with similar thicknesses. The thickness of as-deposited PEALD and ALD Ta2O5 thin films was measured by ellipsometry and cross-checked using cross-sectional HRTEM. The JL of samples 2 (PEALD) and 5 (ALD) of similar thickness are compared in Fig. 11. The magnitude of the fixed charge density Qf = Cacc/ΔVFB, where the flatband shift ΔVFB = VFB − ϕMS and ϕMS (or ideal VFB) is the work function difference between a metal and Si. The C-V data of sample 2 before and after FGA; other PEALD samples exhibit similar characteristics but with different capacitance densities in accumulation (Cacc/A). The decrease in Cacc after FGA is indicative of more interdiffusion and interlayer growth of Ta–O–Si. The JL of samples 2 (PEALD) and 5 (ALD) of similar thickness are compared in Fig. 11. More hydrogen is detected by elastic recoil detection (shown in Table I) in as-deposited ALD Ta2O5/SiOx/Si stack (sample 5).
